# Trial-level accuracy {#sec-trials} ::: {.callout-important} ## AI-generated — not for publication The code and prose in this book were written by an AI agent under human direction; they have not been verified line by line and must not be published or cited as-is. ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## Preliminary & unvetted analysis Exploratory analysis. Exposure counts were hand-coded from import scripts and source papers and are still being checked; see the confidence column in `metadata/exposure_design.csv`. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(here) i_am("notebooks/03-trials.qmd") # _quarto.yml would otherwise make notebooks/ the root d <- readRDS(here("cache", "01_peekbank_novel.rds")) trial_exposures <- readRDS(here("cache", "02_trial_exposures.rds")) ``` ::: Accuracy follows Frank et al. (2025). A sample counts as correct if the child is looking at the target and incorrect if looking at the distractor. Samples with other or missing looks are dropped. Accuracy is the mean over samples in a window after label onset: * **long window**: 200 < t ≤ 4000 ms (the primary measure) * **short window**: 200 < t ≤ 2000 ms A window's accuracy is set to NA when less than 50% of its samples are valid (target or distractor). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} acc <- d$aoi_timepoints |> filter(trial_id %in% trial_exposures$trial_id, t_norm > 200, t_norm <= 4000) |> mutate(correct = case_when(aoi == "target" ~ 1, aoi == "distractor" ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_), short = t_norm <= 2000) |> group_by(administration_id, trial_id) |> summarise(long_window_accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE), long_window_prop_data = mean(!is.na(correct)), short_window_accuracy = mean(correct[short], na.rm = TRUE), short_window_prop_data = mean(!is.na(correct[short])), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(long_window_accuracy = if_else(long_window_prop_data >= .5, long_window_accuracy, NA), short_window_accuracy = if_else(short_window_prop_data >= .5, short_window_accuracy, NA), across(ends_with("accuracy"), ~ if_else(is.nan(.x), NA, .x))) ``` ::: The denominator of `prop_data` is the number of samples recorded in the window, which matches the paper's code. If a trial's recording ends before 4000 ms, the missing tail does not count against it. ## Exclusions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} novel_trials <- trial_exposures |> left_join(acc, by = c("administration_id", "trial_id")) exclusion_summary <- novel_trials |> filter(str_starts(role, "test")) |> summarise(n_trials = n(), excluded_in_peekbank = sum(excluded), no_data_in_window = sum(is.na(long_window_prop_data)), under_50pct_data = sum(!excluded & !is.na(long_window_prop_data) & long_window_prop_data < .5), kept = sum(!excluded & !is.na(long_window_accuracy)), .by = c(dataset_name, role)) exclusion_summary ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} novel_trials <- novel_trials |> filter(!excluded, !is.na(long_window_accuracy)) ``` ::: No minimum number of trials per child is applied (see @sec-data). ## Save The trial-level analysis file is small, derived, and contains no identifying information beyond Peekbank's own IDs. It is committed to the repo so that @sec-exposure-age renders without a Redivis token. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dir.create(here("data", "derived"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) write_csv(novel_trials, here("data", "derived", "novel_trials.csv")) nrow(novel_trials) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 14838 ``` ::: :::
